provenance: hand-labeled 2026-07-16 by eval author from review texts; a GT consensus theme requires >=2 reviewers raising substantially the same issue
matching_rule_for_checker: a SUT theme matches a GT item if it contains >=2 of core_ids; optional_ids neither reward nor penalize

items.summary: Claimed gains are not convincingly supported: error bars overlap on MATH-500, CaT loses to or ties Self-BoN on 4/6 model-dataset pairs, and gaps over single-sample are tiny on the strongest model — yet the paper claims superiority over all baselines.

Core design decisions (synthesis instead of selection, excluding the question from the synthesis prompt, yes/no rubrics) are presented without justification or ablation, making the framework feel ad-hoc.
No analysis of WHY CaT works: is learning driven by consensus sharpening or by minority/novel syntheses? Without this, CaT may not meaningfully differ from consensus-based RL.
Results are hard to parse (no raw-value tables, figure-only presentation) and the text assumes heavy prior post-training knowledge without background.
